catalog_quote: 2.2.4 Stress. Stress occurs by default on the first syllable. If the penult contains a long vowel, then it is stressed instead. If the penult contains a short vowel and the final syllable has a high tone, stress will be on the final syllable. (2.6) STRESS ASSIGNMENT a. STRESSED FIRST SYLLABLE i) [ʕa:lusumo] /aalusumo 'heir' ii) [kaliɁi] kali'i 'colour' iii) [lawala:] lawalaa 'spear' b. STRESSED PENULTIMATE SYLLABLE i) [ʕare:ma] /areema reduction ii) [Ɂafa'ħo:wa] afahhoowa eloquence iii) [q'antsare:ma] qantsareema greenness c. STRESSED FINAL SYLLABLE i) [ʕorruɁumó] /orru'umó sp. of tree ii) [karkarí] karkarí sp. of grub iii) [ne:armó] nee/armó sp. of bird ... [p. 82] Mous (1993: 27) also notes a correlation between vowel length in the second syllable and stress. audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation (sec. 2.2.4 p. 79 with ex. 2.6, and the p. 82 Mous-based restatement with exx. 2.15-2.16) and the domain quotation (p. 222) are verbatim in the Harvey 2018 PDF we hold/text at the stated pages. Deciding source: a 2018 fieldwork-based SOAS dissertation whose ch. 2 is the only modern grammatical sketch of Gorwaa; Glottolog 5.1 lists no grammar or phonology beyond it and Seidel 1900 (11 pp.), and both the author's current publication list and the Rift Valley Bibliography v1.3 (downloaded) show no stress/prosody/instrumental study of Gorwaa. Harvey & Mreta 2016 (downloaded, open) independently supports the weight-sensitive reading: Swahili penultimate stress is nativized as penult vowel length, and a stressed long final vowel is disallowed, consistent with 'penult stressed if long' and with lawalaa taking initial stress. sources.quote: Abstract: 'Vowels are very often lengthened on the stressed (penultimate) syllable.' p. 7: 'Lengthened vowels will be on the stressed (i.e. penultimate) syllable' (filimbi -> [fili:mbi], gazeti -> [gase:ti], kalamu -> [kala:mu]); 'Words in Gorwaa and Iraqw cannot feature a stressed final vowel which is long, as such, words adopted from Swahili featuring a stressed final vowel will be repaired by the suffix /-ʔX/' (choo -> [tʃo:ʔo]).
